OUTSOURCE

1. Title + links

Kay Al Mannai · Yale School of Management · MGT 409 AI Foundations for Managers · November 23, 2026 (America/New_York).

Public repo: https://github.com/kalmanna3i/outsource · clone branch main · 68 tests pass under APP_MODE=demo.

Application: run locally — streamlit run app.py (no production hosting in this submission).

OUTSOURCE is a Personal Strategy & Execution Office: Priority 0 compares opportunity costs and prepares human handoffs; extension modules add Strategic Radar (mission-aligned discovery), Contextual Opportunities (travel-window bundling), and Opportunity Stacking (multidimensional life commitments). All extension UI paths in this submission ran in demo mode with labeled fixtures unless noted as deterministic code.

Priority 0 screenshots are from a demo-mode run on the build machine (demo mode). Module screenshots are from labeled SIMULATED_FIXTURE flows on branch main.

2. Motivation

Fictional persona (not a real pilot user)

Maya Chen is a fictional second-year MBA executive: she leads a small product team during the day, carries a 4.0 credit load, and is responsible for family logistics. On submission nights she faces four simultaneous pulls: a course final due at 11:59 PM Eastern, a close friend’s wedding with a fixed ceremony window, a stakeholder expecting a work status note, and an insurance claim stuck behind an identity-verification gate. Maya is competent; her bottleneck is not lack of intelligence but attention fragmentation and tools that optimize the wrong objective.

Today’s manual workflow (typical)

Maya scatters the evening across a notes app, a general chat tab, email drafts, and an insurer portal—often fifteen or more context switches—with no persisted tradeoffs, no calendar brief separation, and frequent false completion (“the bot checked the claim”). OUTSOURCE compresses preparation into one intake, one ranked plan, AI-only drafts where honest, and one resumable human gate for identity verification.

The same constraint shows up beyond one deadline night. Ambitions are expansive, and time, money, energy, and attention are finite. Achievement and humanity have to fit in the same week. A second fictional person, Amina Okonkwo, is an MBA student at an infrastructure company who also has a dog, a home, a recovery evening she stated herself, a philanthropic interest, and a trip she cannot honestly take during deadline week. The Life Mandate stores her mission and her sentence about success. The software does not invent that sentence, and it does not fill every hour.

3. What is new here

Competition is real. Lindy, Motion, Reclaim, Duckbill, and OpenAI’s agent experiences all help individuals offload work. OUTSOURCE does not claim a green-field market; it occupies a narrower wedge: goal-weighted opportunity cost, explicit AI/HUMAN allocation, and a handoff contract that stops at identity walls instead of faking success. The table below lists only features this repository actually implements (verifiable in code/UI) versus publicly known positioning of named products—without asserting their internal architectures.

ProductWhat they are known forOUTSOURCE implements (verifiable in this repo)Still different here
LindyAI assistant / workflow automation for professionalsNo Lindy integration; local multi-agent orchestration in PythonLife Blueprint SQLite goals feed B01 opportunity-cost objects; not a hosted Lindy clone
MotionAI calendar and task auto-schedulingDeterministic find_slot with busy blocks, business hours, buffers—not ML schedulingSchedules human intervention after strategy agents, not generic task churn
ReclaimHabits, focus time, calendar defenseFixed wedding busy block seeded in workflow; slot search avoids overlapTradeoffs tied to academic/relationship/financial goals, not only focus habits
DuckbillHuman+AI concierge completing errandsNo human concierge staff; simulated insurer onlyTransparent local audit trail (Agent Activity, state transitions) for coursework
ChatGPT agentsGeneral tool-using agentsBounded specialist prompts + JSON handoffs + REVIEW_ALL permission gateInsurer path labeled SIMULATED_FIXTURE; WAITING_RESULT until user_result

The novelty for grading is honest orchestration: public ICS text stays separate from private briefs; F06 resumes only after user-supplied evidence; simulated discovery and stacking matrices stay labeled; one Yale SOM campus address is stored as VERIFIED_SOURCE while hypothetical introduction edges on the network graph are dashed and never shown as real relationships.

Handoff contract

Each specialist returns JSON via LLMClient.complete; WorkflowEngine maps fields into Pydantic models and logs AgentCallRecord rows. Demo fixtures are _demo_labeled; live mode uses response_format: json_object. F03 is gated by REVIEW_ALL permissions; the insurer step is Python SIMULATED_FIXTURE, not an LLM claim.

Radar, contextual scenarios, and the six stacking strategists were tested in demo mode. They are not in the Section 5 bill. The Life Mandate path did make three live calls (S01, D01, Q01) on a labeled dataset, not a web search. Changing an approved priority order changes the deterministic discretionary pick. The model may choose a different id. That disagreement is shown. The mission text is not rewritten to hide it.

Model choice: gpt-6-luna on the OpenAI API

The measured run called gpt-6-luna on the OpenAI API, not the course Portkey key. audit/LIVE_TOKEN_USAGE.csv records 13 live calls. Demo mode spends $0 for grading and module screenshots.

Step-by-step trace of the captured demo run

Workflow wf_e93f8dcd2a05 · final status COMPLETED · agent calls before resume: 7 · after F06: 8.

  1. INTAKE→ANALYZING: user request stored as USER_PROVIDED evidence.
  2. A01–B01: produce opportunity-cost sequence (six recommended steps).
  3. F02: six work packages—three AI, three HUMAN—with explicit depends_on on insurance verification.
  4. F03: MBA checklist + work draft marked COMPLETED; insurance package BLOCKED_HUMAN.
  5. Insurer fixture: returns identity gate (no API call).
  6. F05+F04: intervention brief + slot 2026-11-23 09:45–10:15 before wedding block 16:00–20:00.
  7. WAITING_RESULT: UI blocks COMPLETED until user text.
  8. F06: three follow-ups after resume.

5. Tokenomics

The numbers in this section are the sum of audit/LIVE_TOKEN_USAGE.csv from one live process on Nov 23, 2026 at 7:28 PM ET. The model was gpt-6-luna on the OpenAI API. LLM_MODE=live and INTEGRATION_MODE=simulated: email, purchases, and the insurer stayed simulated. The course Portkey route was not used for this measurement. Cached input tokens were 0. Cache-write tokens were 1058, all on A02, and those tokens are already inside the input count. They are priced at $0.125 per 1M instead of $0.10, which is why the summed row cost differs from a plain input-plus-output product.

Plain product with zero cache-write: $0.004905. Sum of the row costs in the CSV: $0.004931. Wall clock for the whole process: 83.8 s. Model tool calls: 0. The insurer step is simulated Python, not a tool call.

Cost controls

  • MAX_AGENT_CALLS (default 25) stops another completion. This measurement used 13 calls.
  • MAX_WORKFLOW_COST_USD (default $2.00). This process cost about $0.0049.
  • LLM_MODE=demo spends nothing and stores no token counts. INTEGRATION_MODE=simulated keeps email, purchases, and insurers off even when the model is live.
  • REVIEW_ALL blocks F03 until the checkbox is approved.
  • Scores, the portfolio, dinner arithmetic, make-or-buy, the scheduler, and the quality checks do not call the model.

Extension modules (screenshots, honest labels)

Strategic Radar: the discovery feed and most graph nodes are Simulated illustrative fixtures. One VERIFIED_SOURCE edge records the Yale School of Management street address from the public About page; hypothetical warm-introduction paths render as dashed HYPOTHETICAL edges and are not shown as real relationships. Research-to-action can draft outreach (never sent), calendar ICS, a private brief, and follow-ups—Operational in demo with authorization gates. Background monitoring preferences save to SQLite but no scheduler runs (Planned).

Contextual Opportunities: ORD layover feasibility rejects distant suburban tours and accepts a downtown MSI-style visit using buffer math in Python (Operational). The Boston conference scenario compares a 3-night baseline to a +1-day bundle; incremental cost $210 and incremental time 35 minutes are summed in compare_bundles, not asserted by the LLM. Scenario text is Simulated.

Opportunity Stacking: the comparison matrix uses illustrative rows only (not researched organizations). Deterministic code scores strong/moderate/limited contributions without double-counting overlapping benefits and downgrades board-seat career hype. Bundling 18 separate hours/month into one 6-hour commitment recovers 144 hours/year (twelve months × twelve saved hours) only if comparable benefits—stated in UI. Life Dimension agents L01–L06 ran in demo fixtures for this submission.

Priority 0 hours-saved or revenue figures are still not claimed. Extension screenshots document structure and honesty labels, not pilot outcomes.

What teaching staff should expect when grading

Clone https://github.com/kalmanna3i/outsource (branch main), run APP_MODE=demo streamlit run app.py, and walk Daily Briefing, Life Mandate, Strategic Radar, Contextual Opportunities, and Opportunity Stacking. Demo Agent Activity shows UNKNOWN cost. The live token log is audit/LIVE_TOKEN_USAGE.csv. Staff should not expect sent email, a live insurer, a web search, or a running radar scheduler. Background monitoring, a full cabinet, and live purchases are Planned and were not built.
